body.cap: Ninewatt is demonstrating Opti at CES 2026. | Photo by AVING News

body.x: Ninewatt (CEO Youngrok Kim) announced that it recorded a cumulative export consultation value of more than 50 billion KRW with its AI-based building and facility energy optimization solution showcased at CES 2026, the world’s largest IT and tech exhibition held in Las Vegas early last month.

Ninewatt develops and operates an energy management platform that analyzes power usage patterns and rate structures using building energy data to deliver actionable savings. The company assists in energy saving by comprehensively analyzing complex factors such as contract power, peak load, rate plans, and equipment operation methods beyond one-dimensional aggregation of power usage, and by suggesting practical response strategies.
In particular, by advancing AI-based analysis technology, Ninewatt expands its platform’s functionality as an energy advisor, helping building managers manage energy with minimal effort.

Inquiries flooded in from multinational buyers who visited the CES 2026 site for Opti, Ninewatt’s representative solution, and an agentic AI platform for building energy management. It earned favorable reviews for combining a breakthrough level of convenience, intuitiveness, and practicality compared to existing systems. As a result, the company conducted 56 export consultations over the four days of the exhibition and successfully attracted consultation commitments totaling USD 36.126 million (approximately 52.802 billion KRW).

A standout advantage of Opti is its simplicity; it does not require the introduction or installation of separate hardware. As a platform directly connected to existing smart meters, it collects data at 15-minute intervals and analyzes power usage patterns. Its characteristics include providing recommendations by evaluating energy cost reduction, peak load shifting, and the effects of installing solar power or ESS (Energy Storage Systems).

body.cap: Ninewatt’s Opti was selected as a CES 2026 Innovation Awards Honoree | Image provided by Ninewatt

body.x: At the same time, the company maximized access to core insights through a chatbot system using Large Language Models (LLMs). For example, if a user asks in natural language about the cost-saving effect of adjusting power usage by time slot, the chatbot provides a highly suitable, reliable answer through high-precision simulation, along with text and visualized data.

Furthermore, its algorithmic analysis structure, which evenly reflects data such as smart meter data, climate information, rate plans, and building load characteristics, facilitates distribution and expansion. Its modular API allows rapid optimization for various regulatory environments and utility structures.

A Ninewatt official, who achieved remarkable export consultation results with these versatile advantages, stated, “We were able to imprint our unrivaled technological competitiveness on the global market through the intelligent energy management platform selected for the CES 2026 Innovation Award in the Smart Cities category.” They added, “The consultation value generated at the exhibition site proves once again how urgent the task of improving building energy efficiency is in the era of carbon neutrality.”

They continued, “In particular, global buyers recognized Opti for its outstanding appeal in that it is designed so that anyone can easily acquire and understand energy insights without experts or special hardware.” They expressed their ambition, saying, “We will officially expand our business scope into the global energy management SaaS market by cooperating with green remodeling business partners in North America, Europe, and elsewhere secured through this exhibition.”

Incheon Metropolitan City and the Incheon Free Economic Zone Authority announced that they will establish the INCHEON-IFEZ Pavilion in the LVCC North Hall at CES 2026, showcasing Incheon’s urban vision and innovative technologies as the city evolves from smart city development into the AI era. By linking various exhibition programs—including the 10 companies participating in the INCHEON-IFEZ Pavilion, Eureka Park, global pavilions, and the CES Innovation Award Showcase—the organizations will support the participation of 51 Incheon-based innovative companies at CES. Notably, 14 companies received CES Innovation Awards across 17 categories, marking a record-high achievement and demonstrating the technological competitiveness and global growth potential of Incheon’s innovation companies.
